title: Tale of the King Who Kenned the Quintessence (தமிழ்)

keywords: tale of the king who kenned the quintessence
full_text:
A wise King of ancient Persia possessed an extraordinary gift of natural discernment: he could examine any object or person and determine its essential inner quality, whether genuine or counterfeit.

Three gifts were presented before his throne: a magnificent diamond, a fiery Arabian war-steed, and a brilliant foreign scholar who sought the office of Grand Vizier.

The king examined the diamond, which sparkled like a star: 'This stone appears pure, but in its center rests an invisible worm that gnaws the mineral.' When the stone was split, a tiny fossilized insect was discovered in the core!

The king examined the war-steed: 'This stallion is swift as the wind, but he was nourished on the milk of a cow, and in the heat of battle, he will look for pasture rather than charging the enemy.' The royal grooms investigated and confirmed that the colt’s mother had died at birth and he had been raised on cow’s milk!

Finally, the king looked at the brilliant foreign scholar, whose rhetoric was dazzling: 'This man has memorized ten thousand books, but his inner essence is corrupt; he values gold above truth, and will betray the state when temptation arises.'

The king’s ministers were astonished and asked: 'Sire, how did you perceive his essence?'

The king answered: 'When I offered him a robe of honor, his eyes did not look at the embroidery; they looked at the weight of the gold threads! A man who calculates coin while discussing justice has a soul of brass, no matter how silver his tongue may be.'

The king appointed only those whose character was pure, ruling his realm with peerless equity.
moral: True discernment looks past outward pedigree and appearances to judge the inner reality of character. [TA]
